question_text: A service is best defined as
option_a: An intangible activity or benefit offered for sale
explanation: A service is an intangible activity or benefit.

question_text: Which of the following is a characteristic of services?
option_a: Intangibility

question_text: Intangibility of services means
option_a: Services cannot be seen, touched or tasted before purchase
option_b: Services can be seen and touched
explanation: Services cannot be perceived by senses before purchase.

question_text: One marketing challenge of intangibility is
option_a: It is difficult for customers to evaluate services before purchase

question_text: One way to overcome intangibility is
option_a: Providing tangible cues such as testimonials

question_text: Inseparability of services means
option_a: Services cannot be separated from their providers
option_b: Services can be separated from providers
explanation: Services are produced and consumed simultaneously with providers.

question_text: One marketing challenge of inseparability is
option_a: The service provider's performance affects service quality

question_text: Variability of services means
option_a: Service quality varies from one delivery to another

question_text: One marketing challenge of variability is
option_a: Maintaining consistent quality

question_text: One way to overcome variability is
option_a: Standardising service processes

question_text: Perishability of services means
option_a: Services cannot be stored for future use

question_text: One marketing challenge of perishability is
option_a: Matching supply with demand

question_text: One way to overcome perishability is
option_a: Managing demand through pricing

question_text: One example of a service is
option_a: Banking

question_text: Services marketing differs from goods marketing because services are
option_a: Intangible, inseparable, variable and perishable

question_text: The extended marketing mix for services includes
option_a: People, process and physical evidence
explanation: The extended mix adds people, process and physical evidence.

question_text: People in the services marketing mix refers to
option_a: The staff who deliver the service
explanation: People are the staff delivering the service.

question_text: One importance of people in services marketing is
option_a: Staff behaviour affects service quality

question_text: Process in the services marketing mix refers to
option_a: The systems and procedures used to deliver the service
explanation: Process refers to delivery systems and procedures.

question_text: One importance of process in services marketing is
option_a: Efficient processes improve customer experience

question_text: Physical evidence in the services marketing mix refers to
option_a: The tangible cues that help customers evaluate the service

question_text: One importance of physical evidence is
option_a: It helps customers evaluate intangible services

question_text: One example of physical evidence is
option_a: The appearance of a bank branch

question_text: Service quality is
option_a: The extent to which a service meets customer expectations

question_text: One dimension of service quality is
option_a: Reliability
explanation: Reliability is a service quality dimension.

question_text: Reliability in service quality means
option_a: Delivering the promised service dependably and accurately

question_text: Responsiveness in service quality means
option_a: Willingness to help customers promptly

question_text: Assurance in service quality means
option_a: The knowledge and courtesy of staff and their ability to inspire trust
explanation: Assurance is staff knowledge and courtesy.

question_text: Empathy in service quality means
option_a: Caring, individualised attention to customers

question_text: Tangibles in service quality means
option_a: The appearance of physical facilities, equipment and staff

question_text: Customer satisfaction in services is
option_a: The extent to which a service meets or exceeds customer expectations
explanation: Satisfaction is meeting or exceeding expectations.

question_text: One way to improve service quality is
option_a: Training staff

question_text: Relationship marketing is
option_a: Building long-term relationships with customers

question_text: One importance of relationship marketing is
option_a: It increases customer loyalty

question_text: Customer loyalty is
option_a: A customer's willingness to continue buying from a business
explanation: Loyalty is willingness to continue buying.

question_text: One way to build customer loyalty is
option_a: Providing excellent service

question_text: A customer relationship management (CRM) system is
option_a: A system for managing customer interactions and data
explanation: CRM manages customer interactions and data.

question_text: One importance of CRM is
option_a: It helps a business understand and serve customers better
explanation: CRM helps understand and serve customers.

question_text: Customer retention is
option_a: The ability of a business to keep its customers

question_text: One importance of customer retention is
option_a: It is cheaper to retain than acquire customers
option_b: It is more expensive to retain

question_text: One way to improve customer retention is
option_a: Providing excellent customer service

question_text: Customer lifetime value is
option_a: The total profit a business expects from a customer over time
option_c: The cost of acquiring a customer
explanation: Lifetime value is total expected profit over time.

question_text: One importance of customer lifetime value is
option_a: It helps a business decide how much to spend on acquiring customers

question_text: One way to increase customer lifetime value is
option_a: Cross-selling

question_text: Cross-selling is
option_a: Selling additional products to an existing customer

question_text: Up-selling is
option_a: Selling a higher-value version of a product to a customer

question_text: Customer feedback is
option_a: Information from customers about their experience

question_text: One importance of customer feedback is
option_a: It helps a business improve its services

question_text: One source of customer feedback is
option_a: Surveys

question_text: Complaint handling is
option_a: The process of receiving and resolving customer complaints

question_text: One importance of effective complaint handling is
option_a: It helps retain customers

question_text: One principle of good complaint handling is
option_a: Listening to the customer

question_text: Service recovery is
option_a: The process of correcting a service failure
option_b: The process of causing service failure
option_c: The process of ignoring service failure

question_text: One importance of service recovery is
option_a: It can turn dissatisfied customers into loyal ones

question_text: One element of the extended marketing mix is
option_a: Physical evidence
explanation: Physical evidence is part of the extended mix.

question_text: One difference between goods and services marketing is that
option_a: Services rely more on people and process
explanation: Services rely more on people and process.

question_text: One challenge of services marketing is
option_a: Maintaining consistent quality
